key_insight: A simulation-trained deep learning platform can automate interpretation of cell-based HLA antibody crossmatch assays, reducing manual variability in pre-transplant compatibility assessment.
clinical_relevance: By standardizing CDC and FCXM readouts, the tool could improve consistency and traceability in donor-recipient matching before transplantation.
method: Generated CDC-like simulated training images covering diverse real-world imaging conditions.
Trained a UNet-based workflow for lymphocyte segmentation, fluorescence classification, and cytotoxicity scoring.
Added automated FCXM cell-population identification and IgG readout interpretation in a web-based, API-enabled platform.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the automated CDC scoring performed within the range of human inter-annotator variability and outperformed a conventional rule-based pipeline under variable acquisition conditions.
watch_item: Performance was shown on simulated and assay-specific workflows, so broader validation across real-world multicenter datasets and routine lab settings remains important.
paper_title: Simulation-Trained Deep Learning for Automated Cell-Based HLA Antibody Assay Interpretation in Pre-Transplant Diagnostics
